prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1407; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy in force at the time of loss. The driver is a household member of the policyholder and is listed as a covered operator under the household arrangement.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the collision in the same way as in the first report. The claimant has no prior claims history on file for this vehicle.

Entry 4: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact and records the rear-end sequence as described.

Entry 5: Statements taken from two independent witnesses. Both confirm the accident occurred as the claimant described and that the claimant's vehicle was stopped when struck.

Entry 6: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement are consistent with the claimant's account of how the collision happened.

Entry 7: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. Damage is concentrated at the rear and is largely in line with the reported impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known to us or noted in prior records.

Entry 8: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. Vehicle history and prior inspection records show no earlier loss on the rear end.

Entry 9: Claimant's medical records reviewed. Reported neck and back strain fits the type and force of a rear-end impact of this kind. No earlier injury to the same body areas appears in the records obtained.

Entry 10: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Treatment frequency decreased steadily as the claimant's symptoms improved.

Entry 11: Claimant was contacted again and gave the same account of the accident and injuries as in earlier conversations. No changes to the reported facts were made.

Entry 12: File reviewed. Liability and injury information are consistent across all sources, and the claim is ready for settlement evaluation under the policy terms.
